title: Two-property table
subject: Science
unit: Spring 1: Properties of materials and habitats (Alchemy Island and Living Things and Their Habitats)
source: Seeded from science/y5 lesson 12 (Two-property table (portal worksheet))
intro: Lesson 12: Magnetic materials and electrical conductors. To understand that materials can be grouped by more than one property, such as magnetism and electrical conductivity

questions.q: Is aluminium magnetic? Does it conduct electricity?
questions.a: Not magnetic; it does conduct electricity.
questions.model: Two questions, two answers. Magnetic? Aluminium is not. Conducts? It is a metal and all metals conduct. So: not magnetic, but a conductor.

questions.q: Why are wires coated in plastic?
questions.a: Plastic is an electrical insulator, so it keeps us safe.

questions.q: Core: Test 8 household items with a magnet. Then use the table rule (metals conduct) to fill in a second column. Never test plugs or sockets.
questions.a: Pupils' own; steel items magnetic; all metal items conduct; plastic, wood, fabric do not.
questions.model: Teacher shows the first: steel spoon: magnetic yes; metal, so conducts yes.

questions.q: Extend: Which of your materials was a conductor but not magnetic?
questions.a: For example: aluminium foil or a copper coin.

questions.q: Stretch: Why might a recycling plant use a magnet and then another method to sort metals?
questions.a: The magnet removes steel; aluminium and copper are not magnetic so need another method.

questions.q: Big question: are all good conductors of heat also magnetic?
questions.a: No: copper and aluminium conduct heat well but are not magnetic.
